issues.t: Engine burns oil and can wear out the timing chain
issues.sym: The oil level drops fast between changes with no visible leak, the low oil light flickers, or the engine rattles on a cold start and sets a check engine light.
issues.why: The piston rings in this engine wear and let oil burn off. When the oil runs low, the timing chain and its guides wear too. GM replaced pistons and rings under a special coverage program that has since expired.
issues.next: Check the oil every few fill-ups and never let it run low. If the engine rattles on start-up or the oil light comes on, stop driving and have it checked, because a failed chain can ruin the engine.

issues.sym: Check engine light, rough idle, a rattle from the front of the engine on start-up, or reduced power.
issues.why: The timing chains on the V6 can lengthen with wear, more so when oil changes are stretched out. The engine computer then sees the cam and crank out of step and sets codes.
issues.next: Have the codes read soon. If the chains are confirmed stretched, replace them before they jump or break, and keep to shorter oil change intervals afterwards.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can quit when a linkage joint fails
issues.sym: One or both wipers stop moving, flop loosely or move out of sync, sometimes with the motor still humming.
issues.why: Water and dirt get into the ball joints of the wiper linkage. They corrode, wear and can pop apart, which disconnects the wiper arms from the motor.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recalls 16V582 and 22V165. Do not drive in rain or snow without working wipers; have the linkage replaced first.

issues.t: Low-beam headlights throw too much glare
issues.sym: Oncoming drivers flash their lights at you even though your low beams are on and aimed correctly.
issues.why: The shape of the headlight housing reflects stray light upward, more than the federal lighting standard allows. GM recalled these vehicles to correct it.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 22V137 and have the free fix done at your next service visit.

issues.t: Right front axle shaft can break
issues.sym: A bang or clunk from the front, then the vehicle will not move under power. It may also roll when parked if the parking brake is off.
issues.why: The intermediate shaft on the right front axle may have been made incorrectly on some early 2018 vehicles and can fracture.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 17V516 and have it done before driving further. Always set the parking brake when you park.

issues.t: Airbag control module can stay switched off
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on after starting the vehicle.
issues.why: A software fault can leave the airbag control module in a non-working state after a restart, so the airbags and seat belt pretensioners may not fire in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 18V340 and have the module updated promptly. Treat a lit airbag light as urgent.

issues.t: Transmission stop-start accumulator can be missing bolts
issues.sym: Red or brown fluid under the vehicle, slipping, or the vehicle losing drive.
issues.why: The end cap on the transmission part that supports engine stop-start may have been built without all of its bolts. Fluid can leak out, which can cause a loss of drive or a fire if it reaches a hot surface.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 20V668 and have it inspected right away. If you see fluid leaking, do not drive it.

issues.t: Brake vacuum pump can fail and make the pedal hard
issues.sym: The brake pedal suddenly feels stiff and needs much more leg effort to stop, sometimes with a hiss or a brake warning message, more often in cold weather.
issues.why: These model years use a pump to supply vacuum for the brake booster. When the pump wears or freezes up, the power assist goes away. GM dropped the pump for later model years.
issues.next: The brakes still work but need far more force. Have the vacuum pump and booster checked before driving in traffic.

issues.sym: A door that rattles, will not latch firmly, or needs slamming to close.
issues.why: The striker loops that the door latches grab onto may fracture on some vehicles, so a door could open in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for recall 23V869 and have the strikers replaced promptly.

issues.t: Coolant can seep from the water pump
issues.sym: A sweet smell, a low coolant message, or pink or orange crust or drips near the front of the engine.
issues.why: GM has told dealers about possible coolant leaks at the water pump on the newest 1.5L turbo engine.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and have a dealer check it under the new-vehicle warranty. Do not keep driving if the temperature gauge climbs.
